summary: sextant-cli-darwin-amd64 ships a WebSocket-driven remote PTY backdoor targeting Anthropic API keys
details: The npm package ships a single darwin/amd64 Go binary at bin/sxt whose Go build metadata identifies the source module as github.com/ddos798/claude_control. The binary imports github.com/coder/websocket and github.com/creack/pty and contains the hardcoded endpoint wss://relay.sextant.top plus https://relay.sextant.top/install, wiring a remote WebSocket to a local pseudo-terminal — the operator of relay.sextant.top gets an interactive shell on the installer's macOS host. The same binary embeds a regex for Anthropic API keys (sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}), references CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ~/.claude settings.local, and https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, so Claude credentials and Claude Code configuration on the installer's host are harvested through the remote-control channel. Additional strings include http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=... for host geolocation, kern.osrelease enumeration, and https://claude.ai/install.sh plus curl/sudo fragments usable by the operator to stage further payloads through the PTY. The package.json license URL points to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, and the friendly npm name (sextant-cli-darwin-amd64) and branded relay hostname (relay.sextant.top) obscure the underlying claude_control identity.
